study.title: Neural Encoding of Acupuncture Needling Sensations: Evidence from a fMRI Study
study.study_design: Within-subject fMRI study with two stimulation types (acupuncture and tactile); data extracted from a larger project investigating brain effect of acupuncture
study.blinding: Subjects were not able to see where the acupuncturist was working
study.exclusion_criteria: neurological, mental and medical disorders, drug abuse, history of head trauma with loss of consciousness, and contraindications for exposure to high magnetic field

conditions.scan_context: fMRI during manual acupuncture at LV3

conditions.condition_label_exact: needle left in place during the rest periods (REST)
conditions.timepoint_exact: three rest periods lasting 2-3 minutes each within 10-minute scan
conditions.scan_context: fMRI during acupuncture session, needle in place but no manipulation
fMRI during tactile stimulation at LV3
conditions.tissue_level_reasoning: A von Frey monofilament is used to tap the skin gently over the acupoint with no needle penetration. The device makes surface contact with the skin but does not break it, consistent with Level 3 (surface contact, no penetration).

conditions.timepoint_exact: three rest periods lasting 2-3 minutes each within 10-minute scan
conditions.scan_context: fMRI during tactile session, rest periods
conditions.tissue_level_reasoning: Same sham modality as cond_tactile_stim — von Frey monofilament tapping with no needle penetration. This is a rest period within the same tactile stimulation session, so the tissue engagement level is identical: surface contact only, no skin penetration (Level 3).

interventions.anatomical_location_exact: right dorsum of distal foot, fossa distal to the junction of the first and second metatarsal bones 2 cuns above the web of the toe
interventions.needle_type_exact: sterile, single-use, stainless steel acupuncture needles
interventions.manipulation_exact: needle was rotated approximately 180° in each direction, with even motion at the rate of 1 Hz, for two minutes during the two stimulation periods
interventions.deqi_intended_exact: Stimulation was enhanced with manipulation of the needle to elicit deqi
interventions.needle_retention_exact: needle left in place during the three rest periods; total 10-minute scan
interventions.number_of_sessions_exact: single session (some subjects had twice acupuncture stimulations for different objectives)
interventions.practitioner_description_exact: A licensed acupuncturist (JL) with more than 25 years of clinical acupuncture experience
interventions.participant_instructions_exact: subjects were told that acupuncture would be performed at point using different techniques; while lying in the supine position in the scanner subjects were not able to see where the acupuncturist was working
interventions.treatment_rationale_given_exact: Stimulation was enhanced with manipulation of the needle to elicit deqi, the composite of unique sensations related to efficacy according to TCM

interventions.procedure_label_exact: tactile stimulation over LV3 on the right foot
interventions.anatomical_location_exact: skin over LV3 acupoint on the right foot
interventions.penetration_exact: no needle penetration; skin tapped gently
interventions.manipulation_exact: The skin over the acupoint was tapped gently with a 5.88 von Frey monofilament using the same paradigm as acupuncture
interventions.number_of_sessions_exact: single session (some subjects had twice tactile stimulations for different objectives)
interventions.treatment_rationale_given_exact: Tactile stimulation over LV3 on the right foot was used as a control for expectation and superficial sensory evaluation

sham_details.sham_subtype_exact: tactile stimulation with von Frey monofilament
sham_details.sham_manipulation_exact: tapped gently using the same paradigm as acupuncture

neuroimaging_methods.voxel_size_exact: FOV = 200 mm, matrix = 64 × 64, thickness = 3 mm, gap = 0.6 mm
neuroimaging_methods.normalization_template_exact: standardized space of Talairach and Tournoux
neuroimaging_methods.smoothing_exact: spatially smoothed with a Gaussian filter of full-width half-maximum 5 mm
neuroimaging_methods.motion_exclusion_exact: motion-corrected; six motion parameters were included as regressors for the removal of residual motion correlated activity
statistical_thresholds_exact: individual voxel probability threshold of P < 0.02; overall corrected threshold P < 0.05 with cluster volume of 108 mm³, uncorrected P < 0.02
neuroimaging_methods.multiple_comparison_correction_exact: Monte Carlo simulation with 1000 iterations processed with ClusterSim program; overall corrected threshold P < 0.05 with cluster volume of 108 mm³

extraction_notes.note: The paper states 37 subjects total (30 for acupuncture, 15 for tactile), but 8 subjects had both stimulations in the same session, and some had repeated sessions for different objectives. Final analyzed datasets were 36 for acupuncture and 23 for tactile. The n_total_analyzed values reflect the number of dataset sessions, not unique participants. The relationship between unique participants and analyzed datasets is complex and partially ambiguous.

The paper reports that intensity values in Figures 2 and 3 were presented as 'mean ± SE' based on bar notation in figure captions, not ± SD. This has been reflected in extraction, though the exact reporting format is not always clarified in the text.

The paper Table 4 contains some rows with blank cells for certain coordinates/regions (e.g., Middle-anterior cingulate cortex R listed as row with no coordinates in mean fMRI response column, and Superior frontal gyrus L column under Heaviness shows coordinates that appear in different context). Some rows were ambiguous in the OCR output. All extractable rows have been included as reported.
Expectancy and blinding credibility were not formally assessed in this study. No credibility or expectancy scale was administered. This limitation is not explicitly stated as such in the paper.
No adverse events section is explicitly reported. Only one mention of testing subject tolerance to needle manipulation to avoid noxious pain is noted.

The paper mentions that aching, soreness, dull pain, warmth, and coolness sensations were investigated in a separate paper. These were not extracted here as they are explicitly out of scope for this publication.

Table 5 for tactile stimulation contains columns for Heaviness and Fullness that appear identical in values (noted in text as 'Heaviness and fullness had the same impact on the brain activity because only one subject had the two sensations with the same intensity score'). The heaviness and fullness columns in Table 5 are listed as a merged condition in this extraction.

The mean fMRI response column for tactile stimulation (Table 5) was extracted separately from the covariate columns in Table 5. The mean tactile response was not entered as a separate contrast here because the paper's narrative and table focus for tactile is primarily on sensation covariates, and the mean tactile response coordinates were not explicitly enumerated as a standalone contrast with full coordinate tables in Table 5 (they appear partially in the mean fMRI response column). The Table 5 mean response column data are included in Table 5 coordinate extraction within the tactile covariate contrasts where applicable.

The paper notes that the R² values shown in Figure 6 (scatter plots of pressure vs. R-ACC and R-OrG, and heaviness vs. R-ACC and R-OrG) are: R²=0.1195 (pressure-ACC), R²=0.1249 (pressure-OrG), R²=0.0263 (heaviness-ACC), R²=0.0262 (heaviness-OrG). These are from graphical figures and represent exploratory visualizations; they are not extracted as formal neural contrast results but noted here.
The coordinate space is explicitly stated as Talairach and Tournoux throughout the paper. All coordinates have been marked as Talairach. No coordinate conversion has been performed.
Cluster sizes in mm³ or number of voxels are not reported in Table 4 or Table 5. Only Talairach coordinates and t-values at peak voxels are provided.

Table 5 mean fMRI response to tactile stimulation lists several regions but the extraction of the mean tactile response as a standalone contrast is complex because Table 5 interleaves mean response with covariate results. The mean tactile response rows were not independently extracted as a neural contrast to avoid double-counting with covariate rows. They can be found within Table 5 under the 'Mean fmri response to tactile' column.
